# Memory-efficient White test for large datasets

<small>Source: [`R/performance.R`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/R/performance.R) · Help: `?performWhiteTestStreaming`</small>

Computes White's statistic via chunked cross-products rather than fitting the
full auxiliary regression in memory. This streaming approach allows the test
to scale to datasets that would otherwise exhaust available RAM.

## Usage

```r
performWhiteTestStreaming(
  model,
  data = NULL,
  chunk_size = 10000,
  cross_products = TRUE,
  max_interactions = 10,
  progress = interactive()
)
```

## Arguments

`model`
:   A fitted [stats::lm](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/lm.html) object representing the mean specification
    to be diagnosed.

`data`
:   The data frame `model` was fitted to, or `NULL`, the default.
    The response, design, weights and offset are read from the fit itself, so
    a model that transforms its variables, has an `offset()` term, or takes
    its `weights` or `offset` from a column of the data needs no `data`, and
    the model frame of `model` is accepted as `data` (since 0.16.0; before,
    such models needed `data`). Data that are given are matched to the
    observations of the fit: rows with row names of their own by name, in any
    order; rows that only number themselves (a tibble, a data.table, a data
    frame whose row names were reset) by the row numbers of the fit, or in the
    order of the fit when they hold one row per observation. The rows the fit
    dropped may be there or not. Data whose rows cannot be shown to hold the
    observations of the fit are refused; see [test\_results](test_results.md).

`chunk_size`
:   Positive integer specifying the number of observations per
    chunk. Smaller values reduce memory usage at the expense of additional
    iteration overhead.

`cross_products`
:   Logical scalar indicating whether to include all
    pairwise cross-products of the regressors in the auxiliary regression.
    Defaults to `TRUE` and should remain enabled unless dimensionality makes
    the regression unstable.

`max_interactions`
:   Single positive integer giving the maximum number of
    original predictors for which cross-products are generated. When the number
    of regressors exceeds this threshold, cross-products are dropped to avoid
    explosive growth in columns. Defaults to `10`.

`progress`
:   Logical flag indicating whether a progress bar should be
    displayed while streaming the data. Defaults to `interactive()`.

## Value

A `htest` object containing the chi-squared statistic, p-value,
and metadata about the chunked computation.

## Details

The streaming implementation iteratively builds the cross-product matrices
required for the auxiliary regression without materialising the full design
matrix. Each chunk contributes to \(X'X\), \(X'y\), and summary statistics
for the response. The final \(n R^2\) statistic is then computed exactly as
in the standard White test, ensuring numerical equivalence while dramatically
reducing peak memory usage. When `Matrix` is installed, sparse cross-products
are leveraged automatically for large chunks.

Since 0.16.0 the chunks are rows of the design of the fit, read from the fit
itself as [`performWhiteTest()`](performWhiteTest.md) reads it, so the value does not depend on the
size of the chunks but by rounding; the auxiliary design, several times
wider, is built chunk by chunk. Up to 0.16.0 each chunk built its own design
from the formula, on its rows of `data`, so a term computed from the rows it
is given took other values in each chunk than in the fit:
`I(x > median(x))` the median of the chunk, and `cut(x, quantile(x))` its
breaks, which stopped the test ("factor has new levels") in chunks of any
size on a fit that dropped the row at the minimum of `x`. An `mgcv::gam()`
fit with smooth terms is tested as before, on the design of the variables of
its formula, which its model frame holds, rather than on the basis of its
smooths, on which [`performWhiteTest()`](performWhiteTest.md) tests it.

## Supported models

It accepts an `lm` and, since 0.16.0, a `glm` with the Gaussian family and the identity
link, unweighted or with positive weights, a `fitWLS()` fit and, since 0.16.0, a
rank-deficient fit, which it tests on the estimable part of its design: it gives the value of the
same model fitted without the aliased columns. The Gaussian `glm` with prior weights `w`
is the least-squares fit `lm(..., weights = w)`, with the same design and residuals, and the
test gives the value of the `lm`. It refused every `glm` before 0.16.0, because the
checks it runs read the R-squared of `summary()`, which a `glm` does not report; they read
that of the least-squares fit now. It refuses a `glm` of another family or link, a
`survey::svyglm()` fit, a fit with a zero weight, a coefficient that is not finite for another
reason, `data` that lack rows or variables of the fit, and, since 0.16.0, a multivariate `lm`, a
fit changed after it was fitted and a fit with `model = FALSE` whose data are gone, unless `data`
gives its response and fitted values (see [`test_results`](test_results.md)). It stops when terms of its auxiliary
regression are collinear, as the squares of dummy variables are, which
[`performWhiteTest()`](performWhiteTest.md) drops, and, since 0.16.0, with the refusal of
[`performWhiteTest()`](performWhiteTest.md) (see its section *Too few observations*) when its
independent terms are at least as many as the observations, where it stopped as on collinear terms,
or fit the squared residuals exactly, collinear or not, as on a paired design. Which model each
test accepts, and why, is set out in [`test_results`](test_results.md), under *Supported models*.

## References

White, H. (1980). A heteroskedasticity-consistent covariance matrix estimator
and a direct test for heteroscedasticity. *Econometrica, 48*(4), 817–838.

## See also

[`performWhiteTest()`](performWhiteTest.md) for the exact computation and [performWhiteTestRobust()](performWhiteTestRobust.md) for
enhanced reporting.

## Examples

```r
data(mtcars)
performWhiteTestStreaming(lm(mpg ~ wt + qsec, data = mtcars), mtcars, chunk_size = 16)
```
